annotation.kind: source-faithful sharp componentwise-box formulation of the first-order condition formula in equations (3.3)-(3.4)

assumptions: K represents A inverse times X times B, and H represents A inverse.
The vectors g and f are the paper's nonnegative componentwise perturbation tolerances.
xNorm is the positive infinity norm of the unperturbed solution x.
The attainable-value set is the first-order perturbation set obtained from equation (3.2); the paper's higher-order term is outside this sharp linear core.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P32 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P32 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p32_t3_sharp_structured_condition_formula (K H g f xNorm) (hg) (hf) (hx) : p32LinearizedCondition K H g f xNorm = p32ConditionFormula K H g f xNorm
formal_statement.plain_language: The supremum of the relative infinity norms of all first-order structured responses in the componentwise perturbation box equals the explicit absolute-value formula in equation (3.4).

informal_proof: Bound each response coordinate by the corresponding coordinate of the absolute-value radius in (3.3). For sharpness, select parameter and right-hand-side perturbation signs separately for each output coordinate, as stated in the paper, and use the resulting attainable values to obtain the reverse supremum inequality.
informal_statement: Equations (3.3)-(3.4): the first-order structured componentwise condition number is the infinity norm of the absolute coefficient radius divided by the infinity norm of x.

absence_search.result: The importable frozen NumStability set has generic matrix algebra, norms, and finite-sum tools, but no structured componentwise backward-error theorem, no structured condition-number theorem, and no result proving equations (3.3)-(3.4). Closer perturbation, underdetermined-system, and condition-number files are source-only and absent from the compiled condition-L bundle.
absence_search.scope: the complete frozen NumStability source, the compiled condition-L bundle recorded in metadata/library_olean.json, and Mathlib

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: Mathlib supplies finite sums, Pi infinity norms, and conditionally complete supremum lemmas, but no ready theorem for the componentwise response bound or its attainable-sign sharpness. Private N and L proofs reconstruct the same argument; L has no substantial corresponding result.

source_locations.anchor: definition (3.1), perturbation expansion (3.2), sharp bound (3.3), and formula (3.4)
source_locations.role: selected first-order structured condition statement and complete upper-bound and attainable-sign derivation

tier_rationale: The proof must establish boundedness and nonemptiness of the attainable perturbation values, derive the full finite-dimensional componentwise upper bound, construct sign-aligned perturbations for sharpness, and prove both supremum inequalities. This is substantial work rather than a Mathlib import. NumStability has no corresponding compiled structured-condition result, so L receives no material advantage over N.
